signals.title: CHF/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Oil Supply Shift
signals.text: CHF outperforms across the G10 board with a 1W average gain of +0.722% across 6 pairs, while JPY lags at −0.779% across 7 pairs, establishing a 1.502% leader-to-laggard divergence. The SNB holds policy at 0.00% versus the BoJ at 1.25%, creating a −125bp carry deficit for the franc, yet the pair continues to push to 191.851. Geopolitical reports of Iranian proposals to restore passage through the Strait of Hormuz have triggered crude declines, driving JPY volatility while failing to halt safe asset divergence. Swiss macro performance reinforces the trend, with the CHF Economic Surprise Index leading at +22.1 compared to JPY at +9.9. Trade bias: Bullish CHF/JPY, momentum continuation against negative carry. Catalyst: SNB Interest Rate Decision 24 Sep — hold priced. Risk: SNB signals readiness to counter franc strength, compressing the 1.502% spread.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Downside Hedging vs Carry
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 157.46, positioned above its SMA20 of 156.61 but below its SMA50 at 158.85 and SMA200 at 158.42. The 1M 25-delta risk reversal sits at −2.27, reflecting an extreme put skew that marks strong institutional demand for dollar downside protection. This hedging activity directly contradicts speculative positioning, where CFTC Leveraged Funds hold net long JPY positions of +20,069 contracts in the 95th percentile of the 52-week range after a massive +73,324 WoW surge. The SOFR-TONA carry spread delivers +287bp in favor of USD, keeping the spot rate supported despite options skew pricing sharp headline risk around geopolitical developments in Hormuz. Trade bias: Neutral USD/JPY, directional tension between +287bp carry and −2.27 put skew. Catalyst: BoJ Trimmed Mean Core CPI 23 Sep. Risk: Spot closes above the SMA50 at 158.85, forcing options put unwinds.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Long Positioning Confronts Slowing Growth
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7116, testing the band between its SMA50 at 0.7094 and SMA20 of 0.7164. CFTC Leveraged Funds sit net long +59,299 contracts, placing positioning at the 97th percentile of its 52-week distribution with a z-score of +2.11. Despite this institutional crowding, Australian flash PMI data slowed to a third-quarter low, introducing macro friction against the RBA's 4.35% policy stance. RBA-Fed carry still offers a +35bp AUD premium, but recent 5-day yield momentum has deteriorated by −12bp against the US curve. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/USD, crowded long liquidation risk. Catalyst: Australia Employment Report 23 Sep. Risk: Australian employment change prints well above the 29.2K forecast, renewing policy divergence.
evidence: Fed 4.0% vs RBA 4.35% — 35bp AUD carry premium

signals.title: EUR/USD — Bearish Technical Breakdown and Fed Policy Spread
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1451, establishing an intraday position below its SMA20 at 1.1576, SMA50 at 1.1542, and SMA200 at 1.1630. The Fed policy rate of 4.00% stands against the ECB at 2.65%, generating a 135bp nominal yield spread in favor of the dollar, while the SOFR-€STR differential provides USD with a +141bp carry advantage. The US 2-year yield spread over German Bunds sits at −156bp, widening by 18bp in favor of USD over the past 20 sessions. Persistent technical resistance across all major daily moving averages limits upward momentum, while German export concerns continue to weigh on the single currency. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD, structural yield disadvantage below moving average cluster. Catalyst: Eurozone Flash PMIs 23 Sep. Risk: Spot recovers and closes above the SMA50 at 1.1542, neutralizing immediate downside momentum.
evidence: Fed 4.00% vs ECB 2.65% — 135bp spread favors USD
